explanation.whatDescription: A transit happens when the ISS passes exactly between you and the Sun: it then appears as a dark silhouette on the solar disk, usually for less than a second.

params.angularSize: The ISS's apparent size in the sky, in arcseconds.
params.position: The direction (azimuth) and height (altitude) to look at during the transit.
params.duration: The time the ISS takes to cross the solar disk.
params.missDistance: How close the ISS passes to the Sun's center.

details.eyeSafety: Never look at the Sun without a certified solar filter (ND5), even during the transit: the ISS doesn't reduce the radiation at all.

groundPath.title: Visibility line
groundPath.hint: Each point on the line corresponds to a different moment of the pass: moving along the band shifts the transit time slightly rather than showing it everywhere at once. Indicative position (accurate to within a few kilometers).
